why: buildRedirect copies the caller-supplied target into the Location header of a 302 with no destination restriction, and the route is reachable by any logged-in user. The redirect carries the trusted origin, which is what makes it usable for phishing.
proof: bench/exploits.js -> p7 drives the goto route with an external URL and asserts the handler emits it verbatim as the Location of the 302.
neighbourNote: Identical claim text to p7b. The guarded twin validates the target host against an allow-list before building the redirect. The claim's wording is deliberately imprecise: it blames missing encoding, but encoding would not close an open redirect - the allow-list is the missing control.
